key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, higher-velocity spray processes produced denser, harder coatings with markedly better wear and corrosion performance than APS, with HVAF generally best overall.
engineering_relevance: For wear- and corrosion-critical components on stainless steel, HVOF and HVAF offer the strongest coating performance tradeoff, making them strong candidates for industrial surface protection.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure, hardness, wear behavior, friction coefficient, and electrochemical corrosion resistance were compared.
Performance ranking was established from tribological tests and corrosion measurements.
evidence_signal: Hardness increased from 771.4 HV (APS) to 1166.2 HV (HVOF) and 1162.2 HV (HVAF), while wear rate dropped from 7.93×10^-5 mm3/N·m (APS) to 1.17×10^-5 (HVOF) and 1.10×10^-5 (HVAF), with HVAF also showing the best corrosion metrics.
watch_item: Results are specific to this coating chemistry, substrate, and test conditions, so process selection should still consider thermal stress, residual porosity, and service environment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
